issues.title: C86-19 — High: the implementation worker cannot implement or fence files inside submodules
issues.cause: The staged attempt snapshots and diffs every occurrence and generates usable git -C instructions for a directly owned submodule, but implementCommitSteps iterates only occurrences that directly own a task path. For a file in a grandchild occurrence, it commits the grandchild and then jumps to the root; the untouched intermediate occurrence never commits its changed child gitlink, so the root cannot record the grandchild commit. The positive tests still perform the submodule commit manually and cover only one submodule level, so this broken nested worker contract is not exercised.

locations.role: ancestorGitlinkBumps finds every ancestor, but implementCommitSteps emits commits only for directly owned occurrences plus root and therefore skips an untouched intermediate occurrence.
The staged fixtures manually commit inside a single-level submodule; none executes the literal worker commit sequence for a grandchild-owned file.

issues.provingTest: Prepare root -> vendor -> nested with the task owning only vendor/nested/src/x.ts. Execute the literal generated commit sequence after editing that file and writing notes. The current staged sequence commits nested and root but not vendor, so vendor HEAD still records nested's old OID and the root branch cannot reach the implementation commit. The corrected sequence commits nested, then vendor's nested gitlink, then root's vendor gitlink and notes; finalization reports vendor/nested/src/x.ts. Include an unowned grandchild edit and assert its fully normalized nested path is fenced.
suggestedFixApproach: Expand the touched occurrence set to the transitive parent closure of every directly owned occurrence, then emit one deepest-first commit step for each member. Intermediate occurrences stage and commit their changed direct-child gitlinks even when they own no task file.

Retain the staged all-occurrence OID snapshot and normalized finalizer, and add a worker-contract regression with at least two nested submodule levels instead of manually performing the missing commits in the fixture.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: The manifest already supplies occurrence IDs, checkout paths, depths, and parent relationships for occurrence-aware ownership.
Merge already walks occurrences deepest-first and commits changed gitlinks in parents.

acceptanceCriteria: The literal worker contract commits an owned file at arbitrary submodule depth and commits every changed ancestor gitlink deepest-first.
Implementation snapshots and diffs cover every owned occurrence and normalize local paths to root-relative task paths.
An unowned grandchild edit is reported as the fully nested path, and the production-shaped worker-contract regression passes.

issues.title: C86-20 — High: a partial deepest-first merge is misclassified as a zero-progress lap
issues.cause: The staged queue correctly tracks sourceProgressThisLap when a consumed result contains completedLayers, but MERGE_SCHEMA does not declare completedLayers, so the production structured-result boundary does not guarantee that the emitter's progress evidence reaches consumeTaskWorkflowResult. The new queue test constructs that field by hand, while the real nested merge test stops before consuming its envelope into the queue. The implementation therefore has no production-shaped proof that a child-merged/parent-failed lap avoids the stuck exit.

locations.role: MERGE_SCHEMA omits completedLayers even though queue progress now depends on that field crossing the agent result boundary.
The queue regression uses a hand-built envelope and cannot prove that the production workflow schema preserves completedLayers.
The real child-merged/parent-failed fixture proves source movement but does not consume the returned envelope or assert next-lap scheduling.

issues.provingTest: Use the existing real nested fixture in which the child source merge succeeds and the untested parent fails. Pass its actual schema-constrained workflow envelope to consumeTaskWorkflowResult, prove the child source branch moved, and assert mergedThisLap is zero, sourceProgressThisLap is true, shouldEndQueue returns continue, and beginNextLap schedules rebase-test under the existing ceiling.
suggestedFixApproach: Add the complete completedLayers item shape to MERGE_SCHEMA and require/preserve it for ordinary deepest-first reports; normalized pre-walk failures may explicitly return an empty array.

Join the real nested merge fixture to queue consumption so the structured-result boundary, source movement, progress derivation, stuck decision, reset, and next-lap scheduling are covered in one deterministic regression.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: mergeTaskDeepestFirst already retains completedLayers when a later parent layer fails.
The queue already tracks per-lap full-task progress, carryover, and the lap ceiling.

acceptanceCriteria: A failed merge envelope records whether any source layer merged during the attempt.
The queue is stuck only when neither a task nor a source layer moved and failures remain.
beginNextLap resets source progress, and a child-merged/parent-failed regression begins another lap under the existing ceiling.

issues.title: C86-21 — High: unexpected rebase/merge exceptions reject the workflow instead of entering the retry queue
issues.cause: The staged emitter catches top-level rebase and merge exceptions and the workflow no longer throws on a missing result, but the catches sit outside the multi-layer drivers. If a child layer completes before a parent operation throws, the local completedLayers array is discarded and the merge catch returns only status and lastFailure, so C86-20 source progress is lost. REBASE_WALK_SCHEMA also omits failureReason and completedLayers, and MERGE_SCHEMA omits completedLayers, so the concrete typed data emitted by the new catches is not preserved by the declared production result contracts. An exception after the root merge can likewise be reported as merely blocked instead of merged-but-not-closed.

locations.role: Outer catches normalize the exception text but cannot recover completed layers or distinguish a root merge that already landed.
The rebase schema omits failureReason/completedLayers and the merge schema omits completedLayers, so normalized driver evidence is outside the declared agent contract.
The new exception tests cover no-result and pre-progress failure only; neither triggers an exception after a child layer has completed or after the root merge lands.

issues.provingTest: Keep the staged no-result and pre-walk exception cases. Add a nested driver fixture that lands the child source merge and deterministically throws during the parent operation; the schema-constrained result must retain the concrete reason and completed child layer, and queue consumption must retain source progress and carryover. Add a root variant that throws after the root merge commit lands but before close completes; it must report merged-but-not-closed with the recorded merge hash rather than ordinary blocked.
suggestedFixApproach: Move exception normalization inside the layer walks or throw a typed error carrying completedLayers and merge persistence state; the stage-level catch must not reconstruct a fresh data-less failure.

Extend REBASE_WALK_SCHEMA and MERGE_SCHEMA to declare every retained failure field, including failureReason and completedLayers, and normalize post-root-merge exceptions through the existing merged-but-not-closed/recovery boundary.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: concreteMergeStageFailure already converts structured merge failures into nonempty actionable reasons.
Queue consumption already retains ordinary blocked and merged-but-not-closed failures.

acceptanceCriteria: Every rebase-walk, parent-rebase, and merge operational exception becomes a typed workflow result.
lastFailure keeps the concrete operational reason and preserves completed layers, conflicts, source progress, and merged-but-not-closed state.
Queue reporting accepts all normalized failure shapes, including child progress followed by parent failure.

issues.title: C86-22 — High: missingFiles from the third/final plan review is ignored
issues.cause: The staged runPlan loop now processes the third rejection, widens authoritative tasks.json, replans without a fourth verification, and returns the final verifier result. The new regression, however, invokes only the plan stage and asserts only tasks.json, plan text, and the returned files array. It does not assert the required run-arguments snapshot, regenerated brief, same-run implementer prompt, or finalized ownership fence, so the proving test does not cover the downstream contract that originally made the final-round omission dangerous.

locations.role: The final-round regression ends after plan and leaves four explicit downstream acceptance observations untested.

issues.provingTest: Run plan+implement with verifier responses rejected, rejected, then rejected with missingFiles containing b.ts. Capture the fourth plan/implement transition without making a fourth verifier call. Assert tasks.json and run-arguments.json contain b.ts, the regenerated brief and rewritten plan name b.ts, the implementer prompt's ownedFiles/ownedPaths include b.ts, and a committed b.ts edit produces no fence violation while the returned verify object still contains the third rejection.
suggestedFixApproach: Keep the staged verify-then-process loop; extend the regression to run plan+implement through the real emitter after the third-round widening.

Capture and assert the regenerated brief, run-arguments snapshot, literal implementer prompt, committed b.ts change, final fence result, and preserved third verifier result, while asserting exactly three verify calls.
